analysis.title: weekend prep ... 8 Nov 2026 (Brian Garrett, FICC and Equities)
key_insights: Garrett calls the week's price action ugly. Index volatility spiked on Thursday, investors cut exposure, and stress that had been limited to single stocks and crowded positioning reached the index level.
Garrett says Thursday felt bad but was nowhere near the stress of 2020 (VIX 70+), 2009 (VIX 60+) and 2025 (VIX 50+). He reads it as a violent positioning reset, not a systemic event.
He sees more mechanical supply to work through and more technical chop in the short run, but exposures are materially lower and protection was finally chased at the index level.
Trade idea: buy December upside call spreads on the most washed-out indices and sectors (long delta, flat vol, fade call skew). Names listed: DRAM, SOXX, SMH, EWY, MUTM, XLK, URA.

A new metric, the 'multiple surprise ratio' (MSR, a 1-day % change relative to 1-month implied volatility at t-1), showed SPX with the largest reading in 19 years this week. NDX was top 2 and RTY top 5.
Prime brokerage: the global book was net sold, almost entirely by long selling. US L/S fundamental gross is 207.5 (-8.7 WoW, 26th percentile 1y) and net 43.4 (-3.7 WoW, 1st percentile 1y).
Beta-adjusted US L/S exposure is 213.2 gross (-15.7 WoW, 0th percentile 1y) and 57.5 net (-6.4 WoW, 0th percentile 1y).

Single names were net sold for the 8th consecutive week, with the largest net selling in more than four months. Under the surface, funds sold tech and industrials and bought utilities, real estate and financials.

Global tech selling matched the largest net selling in GS's data set (in line with Oct 2026 and Sep 2024). Four of the five largest net-selling weeks in global technology stocks occurred in the last 5 months. TMT long/short funds were about flat on the year as of Thursday's close, down from +24% in June.

The high-touch desk was a net better seller on the week (-$6bn, mostly tech) but saw the first buy skew in semiconductors in 6+ sessions into Friday's close. It has sold $30bn of tech since the decline began, more than July's $21bn.
Thursday's dollar notional traded was the largest regular-session volume ever, excluding opex and index rebalance sessions.

Systematic/CTA signals are negative in about 60% of global equity markets. GS calculates $28bn of SPX futures to sell in a week and $45bn in a month. CTAs have bought $33m DV01 of bonds so far and are modelled to buy another $28mm next week and $78mm next month.
Clients had aggressively taken off protection after Wednesday's post-midterm-election rally, leaving investors underhedged into Thursday. The move in convexity has little precedent.
Implied correlation spiked on Thursday after a 2026 of low realized correlation across individual equities. Thursday was an outlier on 1-day % change vs 1-month ATM implied.

Garrett's Vol Panic Index hit 9.57 on Thursday and closed the week at 9.2. Readings above 9 have historically been good buying opportunities. It is an equal-weighted basket of percentile ranks of VIX vol, SPX skew, SPX term structure and SPX 1-month ATM implied.
'Vol lower' trades have replaced 'spot higher' trades. Investors chased VIX puts instead of SPX or NDX calls on Friday, and the VIX put/call ratio closed near 1.5.
Thursday was the third-largest ETF dollar notional in history, 33% of the consolidated tape vs a 28% average. VVIX rallied 40+ points in a day.

The desk likes shorting a diversified staples basket (GSXUSTAP). Staples trade at about 2x the semiconductor index's 24-month forward multiple, and the premium to SPX and the dividend yield both look overbought. With rates where they are, the short earns carry on swap.

sector_views.rationale: Garrett would buy December upside call spreads on washed-out semis and tech (SOXX, SMH, XLK) after record selling and a first buy skew in semis on Friday.
The desk likes shorting a staples basket because it trades at about 2x the semiconductor index's forward multiple, with the premium to SPX and the dividend yield flagging overbought.
Prime brokerage data shows funds rotating into utilities, real estate and financials while selling tech and industrials. The note reports the flow without a call.

tension_points.bull_case: Garrett reads Thursday as a violent positioning reset. Exposures are materially lower, protection was finally chased at the index level, and extreme Vol Panic Index readings have historically been buying opportunities.
tension_points.bear_case: Historical comparisons to 2020, 2009 and 2025 are striking. There is more mechanical supply to work through, with CTAs modelled to sell $28bn of SPX futures in a week, and the question is whether this is the beginning of something more consequential.
